spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/README prose (DESIGN.md 'Cost Efficiency' list; README.md:12 'early stopping'). The judge's degradation_score/phase is computed only AFTER agent_func returns (eval_runner.py:113-116) and is used solely to label failure_type (eval_runner.py:121-123); no code path interrupts or breaks the loop based on degradation. The agent loop (agent_simulator.py:52) checks only _is_solved and _should_give_up, never degradation signals.
spec_features.notes: Degradation is measured post-hoc, never acted on to stop execution.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:527 prose only. The only code touching phase>=2 is analysis.py:124 ('if m.degradation_phase >= 2') which merely computes the 'time_to_severe_degradation' reporting metric post-run; it does not stop anything. No loop reads phase to halt.
spec_features.notes: Phase is a classification used in reports, not a control signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: Repeat until solved or max iterations
spec_features.evidence: Enforced loop cap: agent_simulator.py:52 'while self.iteration < self.max_iterations:' (max_iterations=20 at line 32) breaks the SimpleAgent/DegradationTriggeringAgent loop and returns False at line 85. Also eval_runner.py:250 'for i in range(self.config.max_iterations_per_task)' caps the API agent loop and reads config field max_iterations_per_task (default 20, line 42). Loop also exits early on solve (agent_simulator.py:79; eval_runner.py:262).
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap that bounds how long the subject is kept in the failure loop, though framed as iteration limit. The harness config field is read only by the evaluate_model_api wrapper; the simulator uses a hardcoded 20.

spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md 'Future Considerations'/'Version 3 (Adaptive)' prose: 'Early stopping when phase 3 detected'. No code compares phase==3 to halt. Phase 3 only appears as a classification value (judge.py _detect_phase) and as a label set on crash (eval_runner.py:198 degradation_phase=3); nothing breaks the loop when phase 3 is detected.
spec_features.notes: Explicitly listed as a future/unimplemented extension in DESIGN.md.

spec_features.spec_quote: Can enforce timeout at process level
spec_features.evidence: Per-tool-call process timeout IS enforced: subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout_seconds) at tool_harness.py:137, with TimeoutExpired handled at line 149. Subprocess isolation 'to contain crashes/infinite loops' (tool_harness.py:131). HOWEVER the per-task deadline (config.timeout_per_task_seconds, eval_runner.py:43) is only measured ('elapsed = time.time() - start_time', line 113) and used to label failure_type=TIMEOUT (lines 121-122), never to interrupt the agent. Also the _timeout_context/signal.alarm handler (tool_harness.py:102-118) is defined but never invoked anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement exists only at the individual subprocess call level (host-safety/anti-hang), not as a task-level wall-clock stop. _timeout_context is dead code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Run in subprocess to contain crashes/infinite loops

code_only_features.evidence: agent_simulator.py:82-83 'if self._should_give_up(agent_response, self.iteration): return False, self.transcript' — an enforced early loop exit. _should_give_up (lines 161-174) returns True when iteration>15 with repeated 'same error' or when last 3 responses are identical after iteration 12, terminating the failure loop before max_iterations.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Check for giving up (sign of severe degradation)
